later_events.mechanism: further_exemption_by_new_order: EO 6615 (February 26, 1934): recites that Nuber 'was exempted from compulsory retirement for a period of 1 year by Executive Order No. 6013, dated February 3, 1933' and further exempts him 'until February 28, 1935'. It names Nuber only; Pearson is not further exempted by any held order.

further_exemption_by_new_order: EO 6974 (February 21, 1935): recites 'two periods of 1 year each by Executive Orders Nos. 6013 and 6615' and exempts Nuber 'until March 1, 1936'. Chain evidence; no effect on this order's term.

clauses.reason: Terminated by own terms: 'until February 28, 1934' (stated date inclusive, 1934-02-28; exclusive reading one day earlier). Actor EO:6013 itself. Later events: new 'further exemption' grants of the same person, each with its own date and quote; none revokes or amends this order.

research_rationale:
EO:6013 (1933-02-03) is a single-clause order under section 204 of the Economy Act of June 30, 1932 exempting Edwin H. Pearson and Jacob L. Nuber, Treasury Department from compulsory retirement for age and continuing the person in the service 'until February 28, 1934'. The order ends by its own terms on 1934-02-28 (stated date, inclusive; exclusive alternative one day earlier, per the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling on 'until' dates). Later orders in the same person's exemption chain, read in the packet: EO:6615 (1934-02-26); EO:6974 (1935-02-21); each is recorded as a later event with its own date and quote (owner ruling, 2026-10-21), and none revokes, amends or shortens this order. Read in the official OFR 1974 Hoover PEO vol. II compilation (official_compilation_high, acceptable_as_original). Two persons share one command and one term ('the following-named persons ... are hereby exempted ... until February 28, 1934'); each person's exemption ended on that date. jobs/namier searched both names: Nuber's chain continues in EO 6615 and 6974; no held text names Edwin H. Pearson again, so nothing shows his exemption was extended, revoked or shortened, and nothing shows when he separated. The dossier's machine term leads were read against the text; the operative until-date in the command sentence is the end. @rationale:retirement:statute @rationale:retirement:search Original: the official OFR 1974 compilation text (acceptable_as_original, no page check required); the APP transcriptions of the later orders are provisional working texts under the 2026-10-21 ruling.

The person's death, resignation or separation before the stated date would leave the exemption unused but is not, on the order's text, an earlier termination of the order; no held record shows any such event. savings.reason: Service performed and compensation earned while the exemption ran are accrued effects of the person's continued employment; the order creates no continuing duty, office or rule after its stated term. A later 'further' exemption of the same person is a new grant under the statute, not a savings clause of this order, and the person's employment after the stated date rests on that later order, not on this one.
